messages:
maria: FYI running long-context INT8 experiments overnight and seeing steady mem growth in the KV cache. On a 24GB A100 the process climbs ~0.9GB/hour and eventually OOMs after ~20M tokens. Profiling looks weird, attaching a tiny snapshot below.

jason: can you paste the pmap / heap sample? curious if it's swap/pager or just fragmentation.

maria: quick paste from the run:
```
[2026-02-18T03:12:45Z] PID 1234 VmRSS: 22.1G VmSwap: 0
kv_cache.total_entries: 12_100_000
kv_cache.mem_bytes: 21_100_000_000
kv_fragments: 1_600_000
pager.page_hits: 0.02
pager.page_faults: 8123
heap_alloc_samples: top=kv_read_copy dequantize_int8_to_fp16 scatter_write_cache
```

maria: note: model weights are in INT8 so base memory is down, but KV storage still seems to be getting written as fp16/bf16 temporaries. The dequant path is creating lots of short-lived buffers that don't free promptly — fragmentation + allocator behavior looks bad.

li: did we change kernel selection recently? we swapped GEMM kernels in the batch path in the last runtime patch; maybe the INT8->FP16 convert got moved out of hot path and now copies happen per-request.

ben: iirc the int8 runtime currently stores KV as the model-native dtype for speed, but the attention kernel expects bf16 internal accumulation. so we dequant on read which allocates a buffer per read. with small batching heuristics we end up doing many tiny reads/writes -> allocator overhead.

eva: quick question — are these runs using kv_pager_enabled? if pager is on we may be seeing PCIe host transfers at tail which look like memory growth while pages are migrating.

maria: pager was enabled on that run. however VmSwap is 0 and page_faults are nonzero. profiler shows lots of memcpy and PCIe stall events correlated with p99 latency spikes. enabling pager reduces steady mem but increases p99 by ~30ms due to PCIe hops.

jason: can you share a perf flame or allocation breakdown? even a sampled list is helpful.

maria: sample flame gist inlined:
```
flame top:
  18% kv_read_copy
  12% dequantize_int8_to_fp16
  10% scatter_write_cache
  8% allocator::malloc
  5% memcpy
```

maria: allocation histogram: 70% of allocs are 128-512B coming from kv_read() paths. that matches fragmentation numbers.

ben: that explains the mem growth. allocator gets lots of small churn and heap becomes fragmented so RSS keeps rising even though logical usage stabilizes.

li: possible mitigations: 1) add a pooled buffer for dequant temp buffers 2) change batching heuristics to favor fewer, larger reads/writes (increase batch window slightly) 3) change eviction to be segment-aware to compact small fragments before freeing.

maria: quick local test — enabling a custom pool (kv_dequant_pool=true) reduced alloc rate by ~85% and stopped the RSS climb during a 6h run. throughput impact negligible.

jason: nice. any accuracy delta with that pool?

maria: none from pooling alone. separate issue: when using the "reduced-quant" INT8 profile we saw ~1.2% logprob drop on summarization evals vs fp16 baseline. seems quantization config matters for quality, independent of the KV mem issue.

ben: also note: our current dequant step does quantize->fp16 by using a fast vectorized path that allocates aligned buffers. if we can store KV in INT8 and implement an attention kernel that accepts int8 keys (or does fused dequant on the fly without allocating), we can avoid copies entirely. that's bigger work but best long-term.

li: immediate action items proposed: 
- add pooled dequant buffers (maria will PR)
- add compaction pass to KV GC to reduce fragmentation on low load (assign eng-runtime)
- tweak batching heuristics to favor bigger writes when context grows past threshold
- add a nightly perf regression for longctx+int8 combo that fails on >2% RSS growth over 12h or p99 latency regression

maria: I'll open the PR today for pooling + unit tests and a microbench that simulates 8 concurrent chats with 1M token contexts to reproduce.

eva: I'll prototype a minimal int8-friendly attention kernel, but it's risky for this sprint. will track as spike.

jason: can we also add telemetry counters: kv.dequant.alloc_count, kv.compactions, pager.transfer_ms so we can surface this in console per-customer?

maria: yes adding metrics now. will attach dashboards for the canary.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot rolled int8-pool-canary to canary host group (canary-3) at 2026-02-18T11:00:15Z — watch p99 and kv metrics.

maria: early canary numbers look promising: p95 unchanged, p99 shows 10-15ms improvement vs previous canary, RSS stable over 4h. will run overnight. :eyes:

ben: long-term note: eviction policy should prefer compaction candidates (lots of tiny ranges) before evicting large contiguous spans. that'll reduce fragmentation induced OOMs.

li: agreed. adding to backlog and we'll pick up after pooling lands.

maria: thanks all — will post PR link and perf graphs in this thread when ready.
